rationale: bugs_open/320. `pages.meta_description` is the sentence Google prints under a page's title, and on this estate it is also the excerpt the blog-listing component renders in each card. MEASURED 2026-08-19: 407 of 731 active pages (55.7%) across 26 of 27 sites have none; three sites are at 100% (loancalculator.co.uk 43/43, adversecreditmortgage.co.uk 19/19, loanzy.uk 13/13). Two independent mechanisms, both still live. M1 (born empty): build-site-planner's `Return JSON:` page object asks for name/title/page_type/nav_label/nav_order/in_header/in_footer/sections and NOTHING else, while upsertPage reads `GetStringField(page,"meta_description","")` — it asks the plan for a key the plan was never told to produce. M2 (blanked later): the same upsert's ON CONFLICT sets `meta_description = EXCLUDED.meta_description` UNGUARDED, three lines below a nav_label clause that IS `COALESCE(NULLIF(...))`-guarded; combined with the "" default, any pass that omits the key overwrites a real description with a blank. M2 is PROVEN to have fired, not merely representable: site_snapshots.pages_snapshot carries the column, and four robot-hands.com pages holding 97/120/169/329 chars on 2026-04-10 read 0 today, all built_from_plan_version IS NOT NULL. Nothing repaired either: all seven writers of the column are create-or-upsert, `default_config ~* 'update[[:space:]]+pages'` over live agents returns 0 rows, and 0 of the 58 discovery_checks name the column. The route that LOOKED like a repair is the expensive one — two `content_rewrite` items filed against missing meta descriptions COMPLETED and wrote nothing (ec701bb3-85e7-40e7-bff1-2ce1ae104861, 13522562-2392-4db9-96b5-204ab67cb999; both targets still 0 chars, and the first page's own updated_at is AFTER the item closed). The cause is ownership: llm_fields/llm_field_specs are per-SECTION and this is a `pages` column, so no writer prompt can reach it. The owner reviewed the options on 2026-08-19 and chose the full fix (guard + planner field + a backfill producer). This submission is the Go half. The diagnosis loop run 7375631a-dfa1-4145-9a07-d13586f1a7cf returned UNVERIFIABLE on its iteration cap — cited as a contributor that supplied M2 and named the site_snapshots test, NOT as ratification; every figure above is first-hand.

plan.summary: Close M2 with a one-clause guard on upsertPage's ON CONFLICT, and add the one piece the framework was missing: an action that can WRITE pages.meta_description on a page that already exists. Finding the pages stays query_database and writing the sentence stays execute_llm_prompt, so authorship remains with the framework (owner ruling 2026-08-06) and this adds only the persist half.

edits.rationale: M2's fix. `meta_description = EXCLUDED.meta_description` becomes `COALESCE(NULLIF(EXCLUDED.meta_description, ''), pages.meta_description)`, matching the nav_label clause three lines above. A non-blank incoming value still wins, so a plan that DOES supply a description continues to update the page; only the destructive direction closes. This makes 'a replan silently destroys published copy' unrepresentable rather than merely unlikely.
edits.sketch:
nav_label        = COALESCE(NULLIF(pages.nav_label, ''), EXCLUDED.nav_label),
...
-  meta_description = EXCLUDED.meta_description,
+  meta_description = COALESCE(NULLIF(EXCLUDED.meta_description, ''), pages.meta_description),

edits.rationale: The missing persist half. Takes a page id (or site_id+page_name, resolved in the same order as UpdatePageStatusAction so authors do not learn a second convention) plus a text field, and writes the column. New authority on a shared seam ships opt-in with the UNSAFE side OFF (owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2): `overwrite_existing` defaults to FALSE, so by default it fills a blank and refuses a page that already has copy. The policy lives in the UPDATE's own WHERE clause rather than a read-then-write, so it cannot race a concurrent writer. It REUSES datahelpers.MetaDescriptionLooksInternal — the bugs_closed/103 guard, whose own doc comment says it is exported so 'a discovery check or a backfill' can ask the same question — rather than re-deriving the brief-vs-public rule. Critically, the result map always distinguishes a write from a refusal with a named reason (empty_candidate / candidate_looks_internal / candidate_too_long / already_has_description), because a successful no-op is the exact failure this action exists to end; a missing DB connection is an ERROR, not a soft {"updated": false}, for the same reason.
edits.sketch:
const q = `
  UPDATE pages
  SET meta_description = $2, updated_at = NOW()
  WHERE id = $1
    AND ($3::bool OR COALESCE(meta_description, '') = '')
  RETURNING id`

err = params.DB.QueryRowContext(ctx, q, pageID, candidate, overwrite).Scan(&updatedID)
switch {
case err == sql.ErrNoRows:
    return map[string]interface{}{"updated": false, "reason": "already_has_description", ...}, nil
case err != nil:
    return nil, fmt.Errorf(...)
}

edits.rationale: Register the action, category `site`, IsLocal true — alongside rebuild_blog_listing, which is the consumer that surfaced the defect (it reads meta_description as each card's excerpt).

Each test is chosen to fail against a NAMED wrong implementation, and every mutation was actually RUN rather than asserted. Flip the overwrite_existing default to true -> 2 fail. Delete the MetaDescriptionLooksInternal branch -> 1 fails. Delete the guarded WHERE clause -> 3 fail. Restore -> green. NOTE A CORRECTION WORTH THE COUNCIL'S ATTENTION: the first version matched `regexp.QuoteMeta("UPDATE pages")` and its comment CLAIMED deleting the guard clause would kill it. Running the mutation showed it did not — with the clause gone the action still passed three args, WithArgs still matched, and all five stayed green. The expectation now matches the clause itself. That is the a-mutation-that-passes-may-have-hit-a-guard-in-series trap, caught only because the mutation was executed.

The whole actions package passed BOTH before and after the M2 fix — the behaviour was entirely untested, so nothing would have objected if a later edit reverted it. Asserts the SQL shape (local precedent: record_vision_finding_action_test.go:118) and pins the empty-string binding too, so the fix cannot be misread as 'the empty default was removed'. It was not; the default is still "", and that is now safe precisely BECAUSE the SQL refuses to write it over a value. Mutation verified: restoring `meta_description = EXCLUDED.meta_description` fails the first test.

Denominator stated honestly: the snapshot corpus is 139 pages / 7 sites / mostly 2026-04-10; 30 had a description, 4 lost it, 10 gained one. That establishes EXISTENCE, not a fleet rate.

plan.risks: BLAST RADIUS OF THE UPSERT EDIT, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: upsertPage is the plan-driven page writer, so the clause is on the path of every plan-built page — 515 of 731 active pages are built_from_plan_version IS NOT NULL. The change is strictly narrowing: it can only PRESERVE a value that the old clause would have destroyed. A caller that intends to blank a description deliberately can no longer do so through this path; no such caller exists today (the only producer of a blank is an omitted key), but that is the behaviour change a reviewer should weigh. The new action is UNEXERCISED IN PRODUCTION. It is registered but nothing calls it until a workflow is seeded, so its deployment contract (DB handle present, page id resolvable from the shapes a real loop emits) is unverified by anything except tests. Registered as SEO-004 with 'built, not yet exercised' rather than 'deployed', deliberately. The action can write public copy. That authority is bounded three ways: overwrite_existing defaults false so existing copy is never replaced silently; MetaDescriptionLooksInternal refuses brief-shaped text (the bugs_closed/103 failure); and a 320-character ceiling shared with datahelpers rather than a second number. What it does NOT bound is quality of the LLM sentence — that is the calling workflow's prompt, submitted separately. Migration 485 (build-site-planner asks for a description) is ALREADY LIVE from 2026-08-19, config being live on apply. It is safe ahead of this Go half: a non-blank incoming value has always won the old clause too, and 485 only makes incoming values non-blank. Stated rather than left for a reviewer to work out. 112 of the 407 empty pages are NOT plan-managed, so no replan reaches them. They are the population the new action exists for, and they remain empty until a workflow drives it. Flagged so 'the fix shipped' is not read as 'the 407 are filled'.
